“Last night at the bar, the buzz wasn’t just from the music—it was in the air every time someone threw back a shot and said, ‘Hey, as long as you don’t get pulled over, what’s the harm?’ In my friend group it almost feels like a rite of passage: you count down last call, down one more drink, then slide into the driver’s seat and roll out like nothing happened.  

Sure, calling a cab or waiting an hour for an Uber kills the vibe. You’re cold, sweaty from dancing, and everyone’s still inside having a blast—so why not just hop in and go? “We’re not hurting anyone, and if the cops never spot us, we’ll be home in no time.”  

That logic sounds so convincing in the moment: it’s cheaper than a ride-share, faster than convincing half the party to stay put, and definitely more fun than pacing the sidewalk. But beneath that carefree swagger lies a pretty stark truth: you’re betting someone won’t get hurt, and you might beat the law, but you can’t beat bad luck.  

It’s wild how quickly “just this once” becomes “every weekend”—all because nobody ever got caught the first, second, or even the tenth time. And that’s exactly what makes it feel so easy…and so dangerous.”
